data.long_meaning: Kali - Goddess of Time and Destruction, Shankar - God of Destruction and Time. The name Kalishankar signifies the God who embodies both destruction and the passing of time. The name Kalishankar carries the meaning “God of Time and Death” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu. Parents who choose Kalishankar usually hope their child will grow to embody god of time and death and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Kali is the embodiment of time and destruction. Shankar is the embodiment of destruction and time. The name Kalishankar symbolizes the union of these two powerful deities and represents the cyclical nature of time and the inevitability of change.
data.etymology: Kalishankar belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Time and Death.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kalishankar total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kalishankar is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology, representing the God who holds the power of destruction and the passage of time. This name holds great significance in various Hindu texts and scriptures, where the deity is depicted as a powerful being influencing the cycle of creation and destruction.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Kalishankar is symbolic of the cycle of creation and destruction, often referred to as the dance of Shiva and Shakti. It represents the notion that destruction is a necessary part of creation, and that the cycle of time and change is a fundamental aspect of the universe. In Hinduism, the destruction brought about by Kali is not seen as an end but rather as a means to pave the way for new beginnings. Thus, the name Kalishankar carries a profound spiritual significance, reminding us of the impermanence of all things and the cyclical nature of the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kalishankar is a name derived from the Hindu gods Shiva (Kali) and Shankara (Lord of the Universe). It symbolizes the supreme power of Shiva, who is also known as Kalia Mochana, the slayer of evil Kali. This name signifies the individual's inner strength, resilience, and ability to overcome adversity, just like Lord Shiva did.

historical_references.reference: Kalishankar was a renowned Hindu mathematician and astronomer from the Kerala School of Mathematics and Astronomy in the 14th century. He made significant contributions to the fields of trigonometry and algebra, and is known for his work on the Jyotirvidyasutra, a comprehensive astronomical treatise.

historical_references.reference: Kalishankar is also known as Kalidasa, but this is a common name in Indian history and it is unclear which particular Kalidasa is being referred to in this context. However, one possible contender is a 9th-12th century poet-dramatist by the name of Kalidasa, who is considered one of the greatest figures in Sanskrit literature. While there is no concrete evidence linking this poet-dramatist to the mathematician and astronomer, some scholars believe that they may be the same person due to the similarity of their names.
